The granted-activation helper has distinct native target definitions, a filter and an output target pair with scopes covering pointer consumers. Generic-spell words become separate aura/graveyard flags, target limit, storage-instance pointer, caller player/card and target-count values. Artificial saved-pointer roles and caller-clobber-style copies disappear when loop candidates/cleanup targets stop overwriting the main instance pointer. Can-cast aura/grave searches retain their predicate/call order and dynamic loop bounds; other control flow and call arguments are retained. The two-word aiStack temporary becomes scalar rv/min_targets; the graveyard player dialog uses a typed old_t0 snapshot and old_nt, retaining field restore order. Native event-specialized source CFG checks all23 union writes and40 reads for partial-word and cross-type dependencies. Native names are vocabulary rather than a claim of unique optimized-variable identity. Complete call effects, dynamic-value provenance and gameplay remain separate. Both helpers restore the native four-byte old_number_of_targets local, loaded from an unsigned byte and restored to that same byte. Explicit native correction: generic_spell now writes caller-context p to td9.who_chooses (offset0), rather than the previously recovered td9.player (offset72). Six native record scalar-event profiles match exactly after the explicit chooser correction. Local liveness and48 aura/720 grave-search predicate classes corroborate the removed copies and loop changes; they do not establish whole-function equivalence. The native chooser load/store window and DWARF location establish p-to-who_chooses dataflow.

loop_predicate_proofs.scope: Complete zero/nonzero/null and handled-ID predicate classes for one aura iteration, and grave-search player/opponent/both/count-sign/shroud classes. Player representatives cover0/1/2/other and the1-player mapping; undefined signed overflow is outside the C model. native_chooser_value_proof.scope: Native p-to-who_chooses dataflow and exact destination. Caller-input origin of p and opaque values are separate.

limits: Scalar event profiles and local type/geometry checks are bounded corroboration, not unique optimized-variable identity or complete behavior. Byte-lane CFG checks retain all non-event branch successors. Native p-to-chooser dataflow is checked in a concrete instruction window; full caller-input provenance, arbitrary aliases, indirect/indexed values, callee retention, other build configurations and gameplay remain separate.
